profile.niche: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym
profile.audience: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym

research_material:
i sit at a desk for 8 hours straight and by the time i get home i just want to collapse. how do people actually find energy to work out after that?
my apartment is tiny so i can't do anything that needs space or equipment. just looking for stuff i can do in like 20 mins between calls
tried going to the gym for 2 weeks and the membership was so expensive plus the commute killed me. has to be something i can do at home before work
my back is always sore from my chair and i feel like i'm getting softer every year but i genuinely don't have time to drive anywhere. what actually works
been telling myself i'll work out for months but by 6pm my brain is fried. need something simple that doesn't require me to think too hard about it

pain_points: Mental and physical exhaustion after 8 hours of desk work makes motivation nearly impossible
Lack of space and equipment at home limits workout options
Time constraints require workouts to fit into tiny windows (20 mins, before work)
Chronic back pain and postural issues from sitting all day
Decision fatigue and lack of mental energy to plan or think through workouts

missing_info: What time do these office workers wake up? (crucial for pre-work content feasibility)
Do they have ANY equipment at home (resistance bands, dumbbells) or is it truly bodyweight only?
What does 'back pain' look like for them? (Lower back, upper back, all-day soreness?) — affects exercise focus
Have any of them tried working out before and quit? Why specifically did they stop?
Are there any 'success stories' in the audience (office workers who ARE finding time to work out at home)? What are they doing differently?

hooks.text: Your brain's too tired to pick a workout. Here's the fix.
What if your workout required zero decisions?
Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.
The fitness industry's been doing this backwards the whole time.
Decision fatigue is why you skip workouts. Not laziness.
This is the workout format gym bros won't tell you about.
No planning. No options. Just results.
Most home workout fails happen before you even start moving.
One question: why are you still thinking during workouts?
The secret isn't harder work. It's fewer choices.

winner.text: Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.
winner.reasoning: This hook speaks directly to the time-constrained office worker by making the entire process frictionless—no research, no decisions, immediate action. For busy professionals drowning in choices all day, the simplicity itself becomes the primary benefit and removes the cognitive barrier that prevents workouts from happening.

runner_up.text: Decision fatigue is why you skip workouts. Not laziness.
runner_up.reasoning: This hook names the specific pain point that resonates with office workers while reframing their struggle as a legitimate problem (not personal failure). It validates their experience and makes them feel understood before introducing the solution.

script.script:
[HOOK]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.]
[excited] "Hey. Twenty minutes. That's it."
[CUT]

[PROBLEM]
[serious] "You're stuck at a desk all day. No gym membership. No time. Your back hurts. You're tired."
[PAUSE]
[whispers] "Sound familiar?"
[CUT]

[VALUE]
[direct] "This workout hits your whole body—no equipment needed. Do it in your living room before work, after work, whenever."
[PAUSE]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Desk job? No problem.]
"Five minutes cardio. Ten minutes strength. Five minutes cool down. You're done. You feel better. That's the whole thing."
[PAUSE]
[excited] "And you can do it tomorrow. And the next day."
[CUT]

[CTA]
[casual] "Follow for more workouts like this—designed for you, not gym bros."
[PAUSE]
[direct] "Let's go."
script.viewer_takeaway: A busy office worker learns they can build fitness in 20 minutes at home with no equipment, removing the primary barriers to their fitness journey.

cover_options: Bold white text 'DESK JOB WORKOUT' on a split-screen: left side shows a cluttered desk setup, right side shows a clean living room. High contrast, clean typography.
Animated timer counting down from 20:00 against a minimalist background (soft gradient or solid color). Text overlay: '20 MIN • NO EQUIPMENT' in sans-serif, modern font.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Clean, modern title card with bold sans-serif text. Soft neutral background (light grey or off-white). Motion graphic: text animates in with quick, confident entrance. Keep it minimal—no clutter.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: Press play. Follow along. Done in 20 minutes.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Cut to b-roll: wide shot of a tidy living room or empty workout space. Natural lighting. Calm, inviting atmosphere. No people or body parts visible.

B-roll montage: close-up of keyboard, desk clutter, office chair, clock showing late hours. Each shot 1-2s. Desaturated or slightly cooler color grade to convey struggle. No person visible—only objects/environment.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: Stuck at desk. No gym. No time.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Single static shot: messy desk with coffee mug, papers, keyboard. Soft focus. Brief pause (2s silence or minimal ambient sound). Evoke recognition/relatability.

Cut to bright, airy living room or workout space. Clean, motivational aesthetic. Warm, natural lighting. B-roll: empty floor space, open room, maybe a yoga mat or water bottle on the side (no person using it). Uplifting tone.

Three quick cuts, one for each phase. Use animated timer or text cards with large numbers (5/10/5). Minimal b-roll of a clean space or simple props (water bottle, mat). Keep it visual and direct—no human demonstration.
frame_plan.on_screen_text: 5 min cardio. 10 min strength. 5 min cool down.

frame_plan.visual_direction: Fade to serene image: sunrise through a window, or a peaceful interior shot. Warm, satisfied tone. Slow fade or gentle transition.
Return to title card style or Instagram profile visual (generic mockup of account/follow button). Bold CTA text. High contrast for readability.
Quick cut back to bright workout space or motivational scene. Energetic final frame. Loop-ready or fade to black with text.

assets_needed: B-roll: cluttered office desk (keyboard, papers, coffee mug, clock)
B-roll: clean living room or open floor space (well-lit, neutral decor)
B-roll: yoga mat, water bottle, or simple home workout props (shot without hands)
B-roll: sunrise or window light (peaceful, motivational imagery)
Motion graphics: animated timer (20:00 countdown or 5/10/5 splits)
Title cards: clean sans-serif typography, white/bold text on neutral background
Color grade: desaturated/cool for 'problem' section; warm/bright for 'solution' section
Optional: very subtle background music (upbeat but not intrusive)
No video of people, hands, faces, or body parts at any point

justifications.clarity: Hook lands instantly (20 min, no equipment, living room)—visual/verbal alignment makes the offer unmistakable by second 3.
justifications.retention: Problem section mirrors viewer's actual day (desk, clock, coffee) but lacks a micro-tension or visual surprise to pull eyes past second 5.
justifications.save_potential: Problem-solution structure with specific time breakdown (5/10/5) is actionable and archive-worthy for desk workers.
justifications.shareability: Relatable pain point, but lacks novelty or ego-driven hook ('look what I did')—desk workers may save it, not tag friends.
justifications.audience_fit: Directly addresses stated pain points (no time, no gym, back pain, tired) with no gym-bro posturing—highly aligned.
justifications.cta_strength: Clear and low-friction ('follow for more'), but generic—no benefit statement (e.g., 'new workout every Monday') or scarcity lever.

weaknesses.issue: Problem section has no visual payoff—showing only struggle (desk clutter, clock, office chair) risks viewer scroll without understanding why this workout is different.
weaknesses.fix: Add a quick contrast cut at 9s: split-screen flashing between 'desk job reality' (tired, slouched posture implied by empty chair) and '20 min later' (bright, energized space)—telegraphs transformation without showing a person.

weaknesses.issue: CTA is passive ('follow for more')—no urgency or specificity to trigger immediate action on a platform where 80% scroll without following.
weaknesses.fix: Replace 'Follow for more workouts like this—designed for you, not gym bros' with 'Follow now—new no-equipment workout every Monday. Built for your desk schedule.' (adds benefit + frequency + scarcity).

weaknesses.issue: Retention dip likely at 4-8s (problem montage) because music/pacing slows without a tease of the solution—viewer may not stay for the value pitch.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten problem section to 3s total (4-7s), then cut to a bright flash of the living room at 7s with upbeat music sting to re-engage—problem-solution rhythm instead of problem-pause-solution.

captions: Stuck at a desk 8+ hours? Your 20-min full-body reset is waiting. No gym. No excuses. No equipment. Press play in your living room—before work, after work, whenever. Follow for weekly workouts built for office workers, not influencers.

20 minutes. That's all. Desk job hitting your back? Tired of the gym excuse? Try this: 5 min cardio + 10 min strength + 5 min cool down = done. No equipment needed. Do it tomorrow too. Follow for more workouts designed for YOU.
growth.final_call_reason: Strong audience fit and clarity, but retention dips at problem section and CTA lacks urgency—tighten pacing, add visual contrast, and swap generic 'follow for more' with benefit + frequency to move it from save-only to share-worthy.
